notes:
**The machine, in Studio.** The Machine block on the Print page now shows what the VP Link
controller is actually doing, and lets you set it: conveyor and feeder speed, feeder mode and
ratio, halt and clear. The speed knob still acts as a ceiling, so turning it down always slows
the machine no matter what Studio asked for.

**Drive faults by name.** When the drive stops the machine, Studio says what the code means and
whether it can be reset from here, instead of showing a bare number.

**Finding the machine is instant.** Ports are now checked in parallel and the one that worked is
remembered, so connecting no longer waits behind unrelated Bluetooth ports. The print service
also lets go of the port when it is not printing, so it and Studio stop fighting over it.

**Help > Diagnostics.** One window with machine state, the full drive fault list, print head
status and software versions - the things support asks for, in one place you can read out.

**A dealer page.** Your dealer's name, logo and contact details now appear in Studio, so support
is one click away rather than a search for a business card. Where no dealer is set, TNR's
details are shown.

**Order supplies from inside Studio.** A real order form: catalogue items with quantities, a
free-text line for anything not listed, your PO number at the top, and a memo for questions.
A confirmation before anything is sent shows the lines, the ship-to and who the order is going
to. **Request a quote** is beside Submit for shops that need a price in writing before they can
raise an order - nothing is ordered by asking.

**Your details, asked once.** File > Settings > Your details holds your contact, ship-to and
bill-to. Studio asks for them the first time you order and remembers them after.

**Order history and a quiet reminder.** Past orders are listed for reordering in two clicks, and
Studio can remind you when you are due for supplies. The reminder is a small dropdown under the
dealer name, and it can be turned off in Settings.

**Postage.** The Stamps.com postage tab, with reprints that go back to Stamps.com and automatic
top-up.

*Note: submitting orders requires an ordering server, which your dealer sets up. Until then
Studio saves the order and offers a copy you can send yourself - nothing is lost either way.*
